summary.text: Alicia Hyndman is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent for NY State Assembly District 29 in southeast Queens, first elected in 2015. Before the Assembly she served on her local Community District Education Council and worked for the NYS Department of Education. She chairs the Higher Education Committee and is running unopposed for re-election.

paragraphs.text: Born in London, England, to Caribbean immigrants, she emigrated to the U.S. as a young child and grew up in Hollis and South Ozone Park, attending New York City public schools including P.S. 34, I.S. 109, J.H.S. 226 and John Adams High School.
Holds a Bachelor of Arts degree from the State University of New York at New Paltz and a Master's Degree in Public Administration from Framingham State College in Massachusetts.

Her education career included posts as Counselor for the Brooklyn College Educational Talent Search Program, Director of Minority Affairs at the New York College of Osteopathic Medicine of NYIT, and Assistant with the New York State Education Department Office of Higher Education.
Worked more than fifteen years at the NYS Department of Education as a Senior Professional Conduct Investigator overseeing adult trade and vocational schools.

Served on the NYC Department of Education's Community District Education Council 29 for ten years, the last four as president, and helped secure $30 million in capital funding for the district's 36 elementary and middle schools.
Was elected to the Assembly on November 3, 2015, representing the 29th Assembly District.
Chairs the Assembly's Higher Education Committee and, in the 2025-2026 session, also serves on the Economic Development, Education, Rules and Ways and Means committees.

According to her official biography, she authored the legislation making Juneteenth observed statewide in New York, and has focused on opportunities in the Queens community through the redevelopment of John F. Kennedy International Airport, small business growth, and living-wage jobs.
Is a member of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc. and the Queens Chapter of Jack & Jill; her official biography says she resides in Laurelton, Queens, with her family.
